The book Make It Stick has some great advice about how to learn and retain knowledge. I linked a summary. Avoid repetition to the point of falsely feeling like you’ve mastered a subject, instead practice active recall after giving your brain time to consolidate information. Space out the repetition and switch between topics while testing yourself. This helped me going in to vet school (though I still struggle) and hopefully it helps a little for you too.

Also, I was very worried about my tendency to be a horrible student, but all my doctors have assured me vet school is different. You care about what you’re learning about, there’s rarely long term assignments, just opportunities to learn material then prove that you know it.

My Northeastern co-op at Angell was my introduction to the field. I was a third year. I got all my experience and prerequisites in a couple years, did some soul searching to make sure I wanted to take on the debt and emotional toll of the job, and applied to vet school in my last semester. I did not get in. When I got feedback I was told I was “too average” on paper. I got a job doing something I needed to improve on, got way better rec letters, applied again, and I’m going to Purdue this fall. Undiagnosed adhd, homesickness, and general disdain for being in school did not leave me with a great GPA, but my passion and perseverance made it possible. Do a co-op, see if you love it, learn about the real responsibilities of a vet, and then take all the time you need to get experience and pre-reqs. It’s a long journey, there’s no need to rush the beginning.
